text:
maria: heads up — getting a steady increase of 502s for hostedapi in eu-west1 since ~06:40 UTC. Customers reporting streaming failures and some embed jobs failing.

maria: metrics: edge gateway 502-rate +120% over baseline, p95 latency up 300ms, authcache eviction rate spiked. lots of traces show upstream envoy returning 502 before request body flows. :frowning:

tom: can you paste a sample trace id? any correlation with deploys or infra changes?

maria: trace ids: trace=ab12c3, trace=df45e6. No user-facing deploys in last 30m. There was an autoscaler eviction event on auth-cache pods in eu-west1 ~06:37.

jess: looking now. quick repro from my laptop shows immediate 502 on streaming completion:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Model: llama-02" 
  -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://hostedapi.eu-west1.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
response: HTTP/2 502
server: envoy
via: 1.1 edge -> upstream 502

liam: seeing identical in ingress logs: upstream reset after 0ms with ``UPSTREAM_RESET before response``. Many requests have large `X-Tenant-Meta` header which moved from ~400B -> 3.2KB after a billing metadata change at tenant side. header size + authcache miss seems to trigger upstream circuit ejection.

maria: repro steps from customer: 1) send long-retry streaming call with metadata headers, 2) rotate token quickly, 3) then 502s cascade. They saw a correlation with auth-token rotate + authcache eviction race.

jess: hypothesis: auth-cache eviction causes auth proxy to do a synchronous backend lookup, which increases auth proxy latency for that tenant, causing envoys to hit stream timeouts and produce 502s. Large metadata headers may be tripping buffering/NGINX limit and causing early reset on proxied connections.

tom: temporary mitigations we can try now: 1) increase auth-cache TTL for eu-west1 to avoid churn; 2) raise envoy/ingress request timeout from 2s -> 5s for that route; 3) patch nginx to accept larger header size (client_header_buffer_size) for edge frontdoor; 4) temporary route heavy tenants to a warm sticky pool. Which one can we do quickly?

liam: I can bump auth-cache TTL in the control plane now (5m -> 30m) — doing it.

infra-bot: auth-cache-ttl updated for eu-west1 from 300s to 1800s by liam at 2021-11-07T06:48:30Z.

maria: after TTL bump, 502 rate dropped ~55% within 2 minutes. p95 latency still elevated but improving.

jess: I'm going to open a short-lived kill-switch to route affected tenants to the legacy auth path (no sync backend lookup) for 20m as a canary. If stable we can extend and plan a fix. @tom can you prepare a config to raise proxy header limits in the next maint window?

tom: will do. For the short term i'll raise ingress `large_client_header_buffers` on a small subset of nodes and roll. prepping patch now.

liam: quick note — logs show a cluster IP handoff race during pod restarts where the new pod returned 502 on first few connections (healthcheck timing). Suspect readiness probe timing + connection draining. We should extend drain grace for auth proxies.

maria: agreed. action items: 
- liam: extended auth-cache TTL (done) and schedule authproxy drain grace increase (30m)
- jess: enable legacy auth route for affected tenants (in progress)
- tom: patch ingress to support larger headers and raise request timeout for that route
- infra: investigate readiness probe timing and fix ejection window

maria: customer update going out: "We identified an auth-cache eviction + header-size + readiness handoff interaction that produced transient 502s; we implemented temporary mitigations and are rolling out a permanent fix."

jess: follow-ups: add alert for authcache-eviction-rate and correlate with 502 spikes, add synthetic test with large headers and token rotate to catch this in QA, add a KB article for tenants about metadata header size limits.

liam: will file GH issue: "authproxy: increase drain grace & avoid sync backend lookups on cache miss" and link traces + logs.

tom: rolling ingress header buffer patch to 3 nodes now — will monitor.

infra-bot: rollout started: nginx-config/edge-large-headers -> canary (3/50 nodes).

maria: monitoring: 502s down to near baseline, p95 latency slowly returning. I'll keep this thread open for the postmortem notes.

jess: added quick runbook step: when 502 surge in hostedapi -> check authcache-eviction, header-size changes, and recent pod evictions. Save synthetic replay for regression tests. :white_check_mark:
